title: A cake for Mother
intro: It is Mina's birthday, and while she is at work Sara and her father Reza bake her a surprise cake. The story practises kitchen and food words, را with things we already know (کیک را، شمع را), می‌خواهند + subjunctive ('they want to make'), and the birthday wish تولدت مبارک. The cake has one small problem – and Mina has the perfect answer.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: سارا و رضا می‌خواهند یک کیک درست کنند.
sentences.r: Sārā o Rezā mi-khāhand yek keyk dorost konand.
sentences.en: Sara and Reza want to make a cake.

sentences.fa: آن‌ها آرد، تخم‌مرغ، شیر و کره را روی میز می‌گذارند.
sentences.r: ān-hā ārd, tokhm-e-morgh, shir o kare rā ru-ye miz mi-gozārand.
sentences.en: They put the flour, eggs, milk and butter on the table.

sentences.fa: رضا کیک را در فر می‌گذارد.
sentences.r: Rezā keyk rā dar fer mi-gozārad.
sentences.en: Reza puts the cake in the oven.
The smell of cake is everywhere.

sentences.fa: ساعت شش، مینا به خانه می‌آید.
sentences.r: sā'at-e shesh, Minā be khāne mi-āyad.
sentences.en: At six o'clock, Mina comes home.
Sara says: "Oh! Where is the sugar?"
The sugar is still on the table.

sentences.fa: مینا می‌خندد و می‌گوید: «کیک شیرین نیست، اما شما خیلی شیرین هستید!»
sentences.r: Minā mi-khandad o mi-guyad: «keyk shirin nist, ammā shomā kheyli shirin hastid!»
sentences.en: Mina laughs and says: "The cake isn't sweet, but you two are very sweet!"

questions.q: Where is Mina when Sara and Reza make the cake?
What is wrong with the cake?

after: شیرین means 'sweet', and Iranians also use it for people, especially children: a شیرین child is sweet, charming and funny – so Mina's answer is a real compliment. (شیرین is also a girl's name, made famous by the love story of Khosrow and Shirin.) For birthdays you say تولدت مبارک to a friend or child and تولدتان مبارک to someone you call شما. Notice the subjunctive after 'want' in a two-word verb: می‌خواهند یک کیک درست کنند 'they want to make a cake' – with کردن, the be- is usually left out. And look at تخم‌مرغ 'egg': it is literally 'hen's seed', تخم + مرغ.
